card.title: Three levels, two strategies — saving variety

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Biodiversity stacks three levels — genetic (within species), species (counts), ecosystem (habitat variety) — peaking in the tropics (latitudinal gradient) with Nepal packing disproportionate variety into its altitude span. Loss drivers chant HIM: Habitat loss, Invasive species, overexploitation/climate (plus pollution). Conservation splits: in-situ (parks, reserves, sacred groves — evolution continues) vs ex-situ (zoos, seed banks, cryopreservation — backup copies). IUCN Red List ranks risk: extinct → critically endangered → … → least concern.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: levels: genetic < species < ecosystem  ·  loss drivers: habitat + invasives + overuse + pollution + climate  ·  in-situ: national parks / wildlife reserves / conservation areas (Nepal: Chitwan, Sagarmatha, Annapurna)  ·  ex-situ: zoos / botanical gardens / seed banks / cryo  ·  IUCN ladder: EX · EW · CR · EN · VU · NT · LC

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: In-situ needs viable habitat size + corridors (fragments bleed species). Ex-situ needs genetic diversity sampled (few founders = inbreeding) plus reintroduction habitat waiting. Red-List categories need population data — data-deficient species wait in DD limbo. Nepal patterns need altitude-zone reading (tropical→alpine compression).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: One-horned rhino (Chitwan recovery via anti-poaching + habitat) vs tiger (territory-huge, corridor-dependent). Endemics (spiny babbler — Nepal-only bird) carry maximum conservation weight per individual. Sacred groves and community forests show culture doing in-situ work.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Classify a case: dwindling vulture populations (diclofenac poisoning) → identify driver (chemical/pollution + overexploitation-adjacent) → prescribe in-situ (ban drug, safe zones) + ex-situ (captive breeding) → monitor via Red-List criteria. Driver→strategy mapping is the answer template.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Counting species undercounts microbes/fungi (the unknown majority). Ex-situ freezes evolution (no selection pressure). Parks displace people without buffer-zone justice. Red Lists lag behind field reality (assessment backlog).

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: From island biogeography: species richness balances immigration vs extinction — shrink/fragment habitat and extinction wins (species–area curve S = cA^z predicts the loss). Conservation follows: bigger + connected + representative reserves minimise the bleed; corridors restore the immigration term.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Levels chant: genetic–species–ecosystem. Loss: HIM-plus (habitat, invasives, misuse, pollution, climate). In-situ = in place (parks); ex-situ = out of place (zoos/banks). IUCN: CR–EN–VU in descending danger. Nepal examples: rhino, tiger, spiny babbler.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB-style: three biodiversity levels with examples; Nepal's pattern + one endemic; loss causes with consequences; in-situ vs ex-situ with two examples each; IUCN categories in order.
